description: Signature edition: Orbital collectors that transmit energy to receiving stations using carefully controlled power beams.
body:

Known science foundations of Space-Based Solar Energy Network.

Solar cells in orbit get ~13x the average terrestrial flux with no night. JAXA and others have beamed microwaves over kilometers on the ground. Caltech's SSPD-1 demonstrated space-to-space power beaming in 2023. China, the UK, and ESA study gigawatt concepts. No system has delivered grid power from orbit.

Key quantity check (Orbital solar flux in W/m^2 / average terrestrial surface flux in W/m^2): computed ratio 8.00588 against the reference value, relative error 0.0007353, within the stated tolerance of 0.2. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Space-Based Solar Energy Network.

Launch cost dominates economics. Beam safety and spectrum coordination are unsolved at scale. Kilometer-scale orbital assembly is unproven.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 7 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is beamed power demonstrated vs target grid power at 7 orders of magnitude (target grid power larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
